2026-11-07-video.caption:
What ISO really changes

At fixed aperture and shutter duration, increasing ISO usually brightens the rendered image. It does not add captured light. Noise depends on exposure and the camera's design and processing.

• Captured light: Set by the scene, aperture and duration.
• ISO setting: Influences gain and image rendering.
• Practical choice: Balance exposure, motion and noise.

2026-11-08-image.caption:
Choose how motion looks

A shorter exposure can freeze movement; a longer exposure records more movement as blur. The right shutter speed depends on the subject, focal length and how steadily the camera is held.

• Short exposure: Can preserve detail in moving subjects.
• Long exposure: Can turn movement into a visible trail.
• Test a frame: Adjust for the movement in your scene.
